newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi, Visco deny differences on Italy mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi, Visco deny differences on Italy mini-budget.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi and Finance Minister Vicenzo Visco denied reports on Friday that they differed over the contents of a planned mini-budget for 1997.

The Treasury and Finance ministries issued a joint statement after newspapers reported that Ciampi had called for structural cuts to be included in the package and that Visco had opposed any reduction in pensions or health spending.

The statement said that "full agreement" existed between the two ministers on policy. "Never, in the source of discussions on preparing the corrective budget in recent days, has this agreement been lacking...," the statement said.
"Reports of purported differences between the two ministers are therefore totally unfounded and devoid of any basis in fact," it said.

The centre-left government is preparing a mini-budget to correct an expected deficit target overshoot in 1997 and try to ensure Italy meets the terms for founder membership of economic and monetary union.
